The 1,876 rock-cut steps get narrow and steep near the top, and the reward is the whole Charmadi ridge laid out like a map.
bestTime: Start right at opening (gate around 6–7:30 am) to climb before the rock heats up.
seasonNote: Entry is allowed only from October to May (Karnataka Tourism), because the rock is lethal in the rain. Winter mornings are coolest; by April start at opening.

trek.duration: 1,876 steps. Allow 1.5–2 hours up and about the same down. Entry window 6 am–4 pm (Wikipedia, karnataka.com); one 2021 visitor found the gate opening around 7–7:30 am.
trek.howToBook: Entry ticket at the forest check post at the base. Fee reported as ₹40 (karnataka.com) to ₹50 (2021 blog); confirm at the gate. Whether it now needs Aranya Vihaara online booking is unconfirmed; verify locally before riding out.

bikeTips: About 88 km via Karkala–Belthangady; the fort is around 8 km north of Belthangady off the road toward Ujire/Charmadi. Combine with Dharmasthala (about 15 km away) or Venur on the same day.
safety: Steep, exposed rock-cut steps with sheer drops near the summit; they're slippery when wet, which is why entry is closed in the monsoon. Overnight stays are prohibited, so come down before closing. No drinking water at the top; carry plenty.

name: Bandaje Falls Trek via Ballalarayana Durga
hook: Fort ruins, endless grass ridges, then a 200-foot drop.
why: You start at a village temple in Durgadahalli, climb through forest to the crumbling walls of Ballalarayana Durga, then roll across grass ridges until the land falls away at Bandaje. The falls drop about 200 feet into the Belthangady side. The walk back up is the part everyone underestimates.
bestTime: October to early December for water in the falls; start 6–6:30 am.
seasonNote: October to early December for water in the falls; the grass ridges stay lovely into winter but the falls shrink to a trickle by December–February. The forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: From Durgadahalli: 3 km (about 1.5 h) to Ballalarayana Durga, then 3.5 km (about 2.5 h) to the falls. Around 13–15 km and 7–8 hours round trip.
trek.howToBook: Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in), Chikkamagaluru district. 'Bandaje Falls' and 'Ballalarayana Durga' are listed as separate treks, each with 300 slots/day (Elneeru snapshot, 4 Nov 2026). Fee reported as ₹500 (Bengaluru Trekkers, Nov 2026); older sources say ₹250, so confirm on the portal. 'Bandaje Trek via Volambra' from the Belthangady side was listed closed. Carry the ID used to book.

bikeTips: Routed to Sunkasale, the village nearest the Durgadahalli trailhead (Kalabhyraveshwara temple), about 128 km via Charmadi Ghat, so you climb the ghat before dawn. Sources say jeeps can go about 1 km past the temple and other vehicles should park at it. Leave Manipal very early, or stay at a Sunkasale/Durgadahalli homestay the night before.
safety: Easy to lose the trail in the grasslands, so Karnataka Tourism advises an authorised guide. Loose gravel on the descent and a long climb back past the fort. No shops or water on the trail: carry 2+ litres and food. Single-use plastic is fined at checkposts. Take care at the Rani Jhari cliff edge. The Belthangady/Volambra approach was listed closed, so don't try it without a permit. Ride Charmadi Ghat in daylight only.

name: Ermai (Ermayi) Falls, Malavanthige
hook: A forest waterfall whose main path may still be closed to visitors.
why: Ermai sits in the Kudremukh buffer forest above Belthangady, reached on a rough last kilometre that ends at a riverside clearing. When it was open, people walked a boulder-strewn stream and crossed a wobbly bamboo bridge to reach it. In 2021 a blogger found the landowner had closed the path to the main falls, and nothing since confirms it reopened.
bestTime: Just after the monsoon (Oct–Nov), if access is open.
seasonNote: Skip in every season: access to the main falls was blocked by the landowner (2021) and it is still listed as closed. Verify locally.
bikeTips: Coordinates and distance are for Kajuru village on the Didupe road in Belthangady taluk, the approach area. The falls' own location wasn't geocodable; sources place it about 5 km from Didupe and 18 km from Ujire, at Malavanthige. The last km is rough and hard on low-clearance vehicles.
safety: A 35-year-old filmmaker died here in May 2018 after slipping on wet rocks during heavy rain. Don't climb the rocks around the falls, and don't swim. The bamboo bridge sways badly, so cross one at a time. Respect private-property closures and any forest department boards.

name: Charmadi Ghat Ride (Ujire to Kottigehara)
hook: Twelve hairpins from the paddy plains to the coffee country.
why: The road climbs from Charmadi village at about 150 m to Kottigehara at about 970 m in a tight string of 12 hairpins. On a clear day you can see the Mangaluru coastline from the top, and Gadaikallu and Bandaje's ridges line up on the way. It's the classic Manipal ride for anyone who measures a weekend in corners.
bestTime: Early morning on a weekday, in daylight only.
seasonNote: Dry tarmac from October to May. In the monsoon there are landslides, fog and traffic diverted from Shiradi; past orders have banned night travel and heavy vehicles. Ride in daylight only in every season.
bikeTips: Distance is to Charmadi village at the foot of the ghat (via Karkala–Belthangady–Ujire). The climb to Kottigehara at the top adds about 24 km (Kottigehara is 127 km, 2h 10m from Manipal). Fuel up in Ujire or Belthangady. Continue to Mudigere and Belur for the long ride, or loop back via Dharmasthala.
safety: 12 hairpins on a narrow road. Buses and lorries cut corners, so stay left and never overtake blind. Landslides hit regularly in the monsoon: a hill collapsed at the 10th turn in July 2024. Past orders have banned heavy vehicles (2018) and all night traffic, with light vehicles allowed only 6 am–7 pm (2021). When Shiradi Ghat shuts, as in June 2025, traffic is diverted here and jams build. Don't ride the ghat at night. In mist, use low beam and slow right down.

name: Coorg Long Ride via Sullia: Madikeri, Abbey Falls & Dubare
hook: Coast to coffee hills in one long, winding day.
why: The road leaves the coast, runs inland through Sullia and climbs into Kodagu's coffee shade to Madikeri. Abbey Falls is a short hop from town, tumbling through private coffee and spice estates, with a hanging bridge facing it. Next morning, push east to Dubare on the Kaveri, where the Jungle Lodges elephant camp sits on the riverbank.
bestTime: Two days minimum. Leave Manipal at first light, reach Madikeri by lunch, Abbey Falls in the afternoon, Dubare next morning.
seasonNote: Cool, dry Kodagu winter with crisp mornings. Abbey Falls is fullest just after the monsoon. Monsoon brings fog, leeches and landslide closures on the ghat roads.
bikeTips: OSRM route to Madikeri is about 194 km, roughly 3h 20m of riding, via Mangaluru–Sullia–Sampaje. Abbey Falls is about 6–8 km from Madikeri and open 9 am–5 pm. Dubare's elephant camp is near Kushalnagar on the Kaveri. Activity timings and fees were not found online; check with Jungle Lodges (info@junglelodges.com) before going.
safety: Sampaje ghat and the climb into Madikeri carry buses and trucks; don't ride the ghats after dark. Bathing or swimming at Abbey Falls is not allowed. Keep a respectful distance from the elephants at Dubare, and follow camp staff instructions.

name: Talacauvery & Bhagamandala (Triveni Sangama, Bhagandeshwara Temple)
hook: Where the Kaveri begins: a spring-fed tank high on Brahmagiri.
why: At Bhagamandala the Kaveri meets the Kannike and the unseen Sujyothi, and pilgrims bathe and perform rites for their ancestors at the Triveni Sangama beside the Bhagandeshwara temple. Eight kilometres uphill, at 1,276 m, Talacauvery's small kundike is held to be the river's source. Steps beside the shrine lead up Brahmagiri to a 360-degree view across the hills.
bestTime: Early morning, as part of a Coorg overnight. Tula Sankramana (mid-October) is the big festival day.
seasonNote: Clear skies for the Brahmagiri view in the dry months. Tula Sankramana (mid-October) is the big festival day and the big crowd.

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online; dress traditionally and expect to remove footwear. Verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Not confirmed online; verify locally.
temple.annadana: Not confirmed online; verify locally.

bikeTips: Bhagamandala is about 191 km (3h 40m) from Manipal and about 33 km from Madikeri; Talacauvery is about 8 km further uphill. Do the Sangama first, then ride up.
safety: Narrow, steep hill road up to Talacauvery, often misty; ride slowly and not after dark. Hold railings on the Brahmagiri steps on windy days. Take care bathing at the Sangama, where river levels change.

name: Belur Chennakeshava & Halebidu Hoysaleswara Temples
hook: Soapstone carved so fine it looks like lace.
why: In 2023 UNESCO listed the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas, and these are two of the three temples. King Vishnuvardhana consecrated Belur's Chennakeshava in 1117, and it is still a working Vaishnava temple, with bracket maidens on pillar tops and a Narasimha pillar carved down to a tiny bull. Sixteen kilometres on, Halebidu's twin-shrined Hoysaleswara wraps about 340 large reliefs and friezes of the epics around its walls.

train.notes: Nearest railhead is Hassan junction, about 40 km from Belur (Karnataka Tourism). Not a sensible approach from Udupi.

bestTime: Belur at opening (7:30 am) for soft light on the carvings; Halebidu late morning.
seasonNote: The temples are open year-round. October to March is best for the ride over the ghats. Monsoon brings fog, leeches and landslide closures on the ghat roads.

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online. Belur is an active temple, so dress modestly. Verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Belur Chennakeshava: 7:30 am–7:30 pm daily (Karnataka Tourism). Halebidu Hoysaleswara: not confirmed online, verify locally.
temple.annadana: Not confirmed online; verify locally.

bikeTips: OSRM gives Belur at about 175 km, 2h 50m (Halebidu about 196 km, 3h 20m), routed over Charmadi Ghat. Belur to Halebidu is about 16 km. Make it an overnight: two ghat descents in one day is too much.
safety: This route crosses Charmadi Ghat, so read that entry: 12 hairpins, buses, and monsoon landslides. Ride the ghat in daylight only. Watch for cattle and speed breakers on the Mudigere–Belur rural roads.

name: Venur Bahubali
hook: A 38-foot Bahubali from 1604, standing quietly by the Phalguni.
why: Long before Dharmasthala's Bahubali, the Jain chief Timmanna Ajila raised this 38-foot monolith on the bank of the Phalguni in 1604. It sees a fraction of Dharmasthala's crowds, so you may get the whole lawn to yourself.
bestTime: Morning, on the way to Gadaikallu or Dharmasthala.
seasonNote: Bright, dry light on the granite. The Venur Kambala falls in Kambala season (November–March).
bikeTips: About 70 km via Karkala. Venur is on the Karkala/Moodbidri–Dharmasthala side roads. Opening hours weren't found online; verify locally.
safety: Village roads with buses and school traffic; take it easy through Venur. Remove footwear where asked, and don't climb on the statue platform.

name: Shishila Shishileshwara Temple (Matsya Theertha)
hook: A Shiva temple whose river fish have been protected since 1930.
why: On the Kapila river at the foot of the Ghats, the Shishileshwara temple's pools hold shoals of fish that villagers treat as sacred and feed with beaten and puffed rice. A British collector banned fishing here in 1930. After poachers poisoned the river in 1996, villagers put up a memorial stone and formed a group to guard the fish.
bestTime: Morning, after Dharmasthala or Sowthadka; Kokkada is the turn-off.
seasonNote: Lower dry-season water makes the sacred fish easier to see in the clear pools. In the monsoon the Kapila river runs high.

temple.dressCode: Not confirmed online; verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Not confirmed online; verify locally.
temple.annadana: Not confirmed online; verify locally.

bikeTips: About 121 km. Wikipedia notes buses from Dharmasthala or Uppinangady stop near the temple, or reach Kokkada and take a jeep or auto. On a bike, ride via Kokkada.
safety: Fishing is banned. Feed the fish only beaten rice or puffed rice, never packaged food. River-edge steps get slippery; don't wade in.

name: Agumbe Ghat & Sunset Point
hook: Hairpins up, sun down, the whole coast laid out below.
why: The Agumbe ghat on NH 169A is the classic Manipal ride: a staircase of hairpins climbing out of the coastal heat into Malnad mist. At the top, the Sunset Point sits right on the highway and, on a clear evening, the sun drops into the Arabian Sea. Agumbe itself gets around 7,500 mm of rain a year, which explains why everything here is green, mossy and dripping.
bestTime: Clear winter evenings, November to February; get there before sunset because it fills up in season.
seasonNote: November to February for a proper sea sunset. Agumbe is one of the wettest places in India: in the monsoon the view is mostly cloud, the ghat is foggy, and heavy vehicles are banned (2026: from 15 June).
bikeTips: Ride time is the OSRM estimate plus a buffer; the hairpin section is slower than it looks, so add time if you stop for photos. The Sunset Point is on the highway, so you can ride right up to it. Agumbe village, where much of Malgudi Days was shot, is about a ten-minute walk from the point (Wikipedia). Leave the viewpoint as soon as the sun goes down, or plan to sleep in Agumbe rather than descend in the dark.
safety: Ghat road: tight hairpins, blind corners, buses and trucks swinging wide. Hold your lane and use the horn on blind bends. Fog can roll in fast and evening mist on the descent makes the surface greasy. Avoid riding down after dark. Heavy vehicles are banned on this ghat during the monsoon (June–September/October in recent years) because of landslide risk; outside that window expect trucks. The Agumbe Rainforest Research Station is a working research station (founded in 2005 by Romulus Whitaker), not a visitor attraction. We found no public visiting info, so don't just turn up. King cobra country: stay on paths if you walk into the forest.

name: Kudlu Theertha Falls
hook: A rainbow-throwing plunge pool, two stream crossings in.
why: Inside Someshwara Wildlife Sanctuary, Kudlu Theertha drops into a wide pool, and on a sunny morning the spray throws rainbows. The walk in is about 2 km of mostly paved path with 150–200 steps and two streams to wade. It's the falls locals rate for December, if the forest gate is open.
bestTime: Post-monsoon mornings. A 2021–24 visitor blog rates December–January best, when the falls are open.
seasonNote: Post-monsoon to December, while there's water and the trail is open. It's in Someshwara sanctuary, so the forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: About 2–2.5 km each way from the entry gate (roughly 30 minutes), with 150–200 steps and two stream crossings
trek.howToBook: A visitor blog (Nov 2024 update) says online registration is now required and you still fill in details and pay cash at the counter. The portal isn't named. Verify locally.

bikeTips: Coordinates and distance are for Kudlu Falls Road, the OSM-mapped access road off the Hebri–Agumbe side, not the falls. A blog notes the last ~3 km to the gate was rough in 2022, with loose gravel and steep bits. Go slow on a loaded bike. Reported fees (2024): ₹100 per person, ₹15 bike parking, ₹300 for a camera. Verify locally.
safety: Two stream crossings on the walk; skip them if the water is high. Wet rocks around the pool are slippery. Leeches were reported as late as November. Gates reportedly open around 9–9:30 AM and you must be out by 4 PM, so start walking by about 2 PM. The forest department closes the falls when elephants or other wild animals are spotted, and trekking in this sanctuary was banned from 14 Jan 2026 for fire risk. Verify the current status locally.

name: Barkana Falls & Viewpoint
hook: One of India's tallest falls, seen across a whole valley.
why: Karnataka Tourism puts the Seetha River's drop at Barkana at about 260 m, which makes it one of India's tallest falls. Most people see it from the Barkana viewpoint: an easy 2 km forest walk from a forest gate past Jogi Gundi that ends with the falls threading down a distant cliff and the Agumbe valley falling away below. Getting to the falls themselves is a proper forest trek that needs permission and a guide.
bestTime: October to February per Karnataka Tourism; early mornings can be fogged in.
seasonNote: October to February per Karnataka Tourism; the falls are biggest right after the rains. Mornings can be fogged in.

trek.duration: Viewpoint: about 2 km easy walk from the forest gate. The falls trek is separate and longer.
trek.howToBook: Viewpoint: pay at the forest check post near the Jogi Gundi turn (a 2022 blog says about ₹100 per person plus camera and parking). The trek to the falls needs prior Forest Department permission and a guided trek is strongly advised. Booking route not confirmed online, so verify locally.

bikeTips: We couldn't get reliable coordinates for the viewpoint, so lat/lng and distance are left null. For planning, Jogi Gundi is 51 km / about 45 min from Manipal (OSRM). From Agumbe take the Sringeri road, turn off for Jogi Gundi after about 1 km, carry on a few km past houses, turn right at the sign and ride about 2 km to the forest gate (2022 directions). The road was under repair but car-friendly then.
safety: Fog can hide the falls completely, especially early morning. If you do the falls trek, the rocks at the top of Barkana on the Seetha River are very slippery. Stay well back from the edge. Leeches after rain. Don't trek to the falls without permission. It's sensitive forest.

name: Jogi Gundi Falls
hook: Agumbe's pocket waterfall, best caught right after the rains.
why: A short forest walk and about 300 m of steps drop you to a deep pool under a forest waterfall. It's close to Agumbe and pairs easily with the Barkana viewpoint. In monsoon it roars. By late autumn it's down to a trickle.
bestTime: July to October (visitor blog). Entry is restricted in heavy monsoon rain.
seasonNote: A monsoon fall, best from July to October; nearly dry by November. Entry is restricted in heavy rain.
bikeTips: From Agumbe, take the Sringeri road and turn off after about 1 km. Then it's about 1 km on foot: 300–500 m on the flat, then steps down. A blog lists 9 AM–5 PM hours (gate shut if you come early) and ₹100 per person. Some sites say entry is free, so verify locally. No facilities at the site. Agumbe town is about 4 km away.
safety: The pool is too deep to stand under the fall. If you get in, stay at the edges. Wet steps and rocks are slippery. Entry is restricted during heavy monsoon rain.

name: Varanga Kere Basadi (Lake Temple)
hook: A four-faced Jain shrine you can only reach by boat.
why: A 12th-century chaturmukha basadi sits alone in a lily-covered lake. Parshvanatha, Neminatha, Shantinatha and Anantanatha face the four directions, and a short boat ride is the only way in. Ashore, the 9th-century Neminatha Basadi has a 45-foot monolithic manastambha. It's 35 minutes from Manipal and feels a century further away.
bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon, inside the boat hours.
seasonNote: Not seasonal: the boat runs year-round. Cool mornings and water lilies make winter the prettiest. Boat hours: verify locally.

temple.darshanTimings: Boat to Kere Basadi: 8:30 AM–1 PM and 3–6 PM (Holidify); other listings give 4–6 PM for the evening session. Verify locally.

bikeTips: Straight run up the Hebri side of the Udupi–Agumbe road, all on good highway (Varanga sits on SH1 per OSM). The boat is about 100 m and costs ₹10 (karnataka.com, Holidify).
safety: Short boat crossing. Sit still and follow the boatman. Basadi etiquette applies: footwear off, dress modestly (no official dress code found online, so verify locally).

name: Sringeri Sharada Peetham
hook: Adi Shankara's southern seat, with lunch for thousands daily.
why: The Dakshinamnaya Sharada Peetham is one of the four mathas Adi Shankaracharya founded, set on the Tunga with the Sharadamba temple at its heart. Next door, the Vidyashankara temple blends Hoysala and Vijayanagara styles and has zodiac carvings. The Peetham's dining hall serves Nitya Annadana to about 7,500 people a day.
bestTime: October to March (Karnataka Tourism). Arrive for the morning darshan and stay for lunch.
seasonNote: Open year-round; October to March per Karnataka Tourism for weather. Navaratri (Sharada Sharannavaratri) is the big festival. Monsoon brings fog, leeches and landslide closures on the ghat roads. That applies to the Agumbe approach.

temple.dressCode: Modest, traditional dress (Karnataka Tourism: 'modest dressing is advised'; Yatradham: traditional and formal clothing). The Peetham's own detailed dress-code notice isn't readable online. Verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: Sharadamba temple: 6 AM–2 PM and 4–9 PM. Maha-Mangalarati at 10 AM, 12 noon and 7:30 PM. Other temples: 6 AM–1 PM and 5–8 PM. Guru Darshanam 10:30–11:30 AM. Chandramoulishwara Puja by the Jagadguru 9–10 PM (8:30–10 PM on Fridays). Timings change with events and the Jagadguru's camps (official site).
temple.annadana: Nitya Annadana at the Sri Bharathi Theertha Prasada hall near the Sharada temple: 12:15–2:30 PM and 7:15–8:30 PM (official site).

bikeTips: The ride climbs the Agumbe ghat, so do the hairpins in daylight. Guest houses near the temple go first-come-first-served, with no advance booking. Ask at the Information Office by the main entrance.
safety: Agumbe ghat hairpins on the way: avoid descending after dark and watch for buses. Photography is not allowed inside the temple (Yatradham). Respect queue and silence rules.

name: Horanadu Annapoorneshwari Temple
hook: The goddess of food, and she means it: everyone eats.
why: Annapoorneshwari stands in gold on the Bhadra's banks, deep in Western Ghats forest. Pilgrims get free meals three times a day, plus tea or coffee and snacks, whatever their religion or caste. Men take their shirts off for the darshan line, so bring a shawl or towel.
bestTime: Any season. Reach for the morning darshan and stay through lunch.
seasonNote: Any season. Clear roads and cool forest air in winter; heavy rain and the odd landslide on the Kalasa roads in the monsoon.
vegFoodNearby: Temple annadana hall (on site): free vegetarian meals for all pilgrims, served afternoon and evening (templesinindiainfo; Karnataka Tourism says three times a day).

temple.dressCode: Men: full pants, pancha or dhoti. Shirts must come off for the darshan line, and a towel or shawl over the shoulders is fine (Holidify, Trawell, templesinindiainfo). Women: saree, salwar or other modest traditional wear. These are third-party listings, so verify locally.
temple.darshanTimings: 6:30–9 AM, 11 AM–2 PM, 7–9:30 PM daily (Holidify, Trawell, templesinindiainfo). Third-party listings, so verify locally.
temple.annadana: Free meals three times a day, including tea, coffee and snacks, open to all (Karnataka Tourism). Prasada Bhojana listed as 12 noon–3 PM and 7:30–9:30 PM (templesinindiainfo). Verify locally.

bikeTips: Ride time is OSRM plus buffer. The road climbs into the ghats via Kalasa, with forest stretches and narrow sections, so start early and be back on the plains before dark.
safety: Ghat and forest roads with narrow bends and buses. Avoid riding them at night. Watch for wildlife crossing in forest sections.

name: Kudremukh Peak Trek
hook: Karnataka's signature trek: 16 km of grass, shola and sky.
why: The 'horse face' peak (1,867 m) gives its name to the whole national park. The trail rolls through shola forest, streams and miles of open grassland to a summit that once guided sailors along the coast. IndiaHikes calls it the most iconic trek in Karnataka, and it's a full, honest day on your legs.
bestTime: Post-monsoon to early winter, when the grass is green and the skies are clear.
seasonNote: Post-monsoon to December, when the grass is green and skies are clear. The forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: Full day, about 16 km return. Start from the Mullodi forest office by 7:30 AM to summit around noon. Turn back by 2 PM at the latest and you'll be down around 4:30 PM (IndiaHikes).
trek.howToBook: Book on the Karnataka Forest Dept's Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in). Portal rules effective 15 Jul 2026: slots open up to 30 days ahead and must be booked at least 1 day ahead; cancel 8+ days out for a 50% refund, nothing back within 7 days; carry the original ID you booked with and report 10 minutes before your slot. Helpline 1926. Listed under Chikkamagaluru district treks. One blog reports a 2026 cap of 50 trekkers a day, but other reports conflict, so check the portal.

bikeTips: Distance and time are to Mullodi, the trailhead locality with the forest office, routed via Karkala and SH66. The peak coordinates are in lat/lng. Ride up the day before and sleep at a Mullodi homestay. IndiaHikes says homestays there do breakfast and a packed lunch (about ₹200) if you book ahead. Camping on the trek isn't allowed.
safety: Forest sections are slippery, and mossy rocks at stream crossings are worse. Wear real trekking shoes. Stay on the marked trail. Flash photography and single-use plastic are banned in the trekking zones under the 2026 SOP. Last season the Kudremukh Wildlife Division shut every trekking route in Kudremukh NP, Someshwara and Mookambika sanctuaries from 14 January 2026 for forest-fire risk, 'until further notice'. The final ~3 km from the second Ontimara is a steep, sustained climb. Turn around on time, because getting stuck after dark in a national park is a real risk. Guides are mandatory: one per 10 trekkers, about ₹1,000 per guide (IndiaHikes).

name: Netravati Peak Trek
hook: Kudremukh's shorter sibling, and harder to book than to climb.
why: Netravati (about 1,520 m) sits on the Chikkamagaluru–Dakshina Kannada border inside Kudremukh National Park. It's a gentler 12–14 km day through forest and open meadow. It got so popular that slots now reportedly vanish within a minute of opening.
bestTime: Post-monsoon to early winter.
seasonNote: Post-monsoon to December. The forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: Full day, about 12–14 km round trip (2026 blog estimate). Verify locally.
trek.howToBook: Book on the Karnataka Forest Dept's Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in). Portal rules effective 15 Jul 2026: slots open up to 30 days ahead and must be booked at least 1 day ahead; cancel 8+ days out for a 50% refund, nothing back within 7 days; carry the original ID you booked with and report 10 minutes before your slot. Helpline 1926. No offline permits. One 2026 blog reports a 50-a-day cap with slots opening at midnight and selling out within a minute. That's unconfirmed, so check the portal.

bikeTips: Distance and time are to Samse village, the base about 14 km from Kalasa (2026 blog). The peak coordinates are in lat/lng. Stay overnight near Samse or Kalasa so you're at the start early. Horanadu temple fits on the same trip.
safety: Forest sections are slippery, and mossy rocks at stream crossings are worse. Wear real trekking shoes. Stay on the marked trail. Flash photography and single-use plastic are banned in the trekking zones under the 2026 SOP. Last season the Kudremukh Wildlife Division shut every trekking route in Kudremukh NP, Someshwara and Mookambika sanctuaries from 14 January 2026 for forest-fire risk, 'until further notice'. Guides are compulsory: one per batch of 10 under the 2026 SOP.

name: Kurinjal Peak Trek
hook: Dense evergreen forest, then a grandstand view of Kudremukh.
why: Kurinjal starts at Bhagavathi Nature Camp and climbs through evergreen forest loud with birds before opening onto a huge grassy clearing. From the top you look straight across at Kudremukh peak. It's the trek people switch to when Kudremukh slots are gone, and a visitor says only the last kilometre is properly steep.
bestTime: Post-monsoon to winter. IndiaHikes advises against peak summer because the upper section is exposed.
seasonNote: Post-monsoon to December; IndiaHikes advises against peak summer because the top is exposed. The forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: About 12–16 km round trip depending on source. Plan a full day.
trek.howToBook: Book on the Karnataka Forest Dept's Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in). Portal rules effective 15 Jul 2026: slots open up to 30 days ahead and must be booked at least 1 day ahead; cancel 8+ days out for a 50% refund, nothing back within 7 days; carry the original ID you booked with and report 10 minutes before your slot. Helpline 1926. Older IndiaHikes notes mention a forest office at the Bhagavathi Nature Camp entrance, where bags are checked for plastic and packaged food.

bikeTips: Distance and time are to Bhagavathi Nature Camp, the trailhead about 29 km from Kalasa on SH66, routed via Karkala. The peak coordinates are in lat/lng. It works as a long day from Manipal if you leave at dawn. The trail gate is about 500 m along the highway from the forest office.
safety: Forest sections are slippery, and mossy rocks at stream crossings are worse. Wear real trekking shoes. Stay on the marked trail. Flash photography and single-use plastic are banned in the trekking zones under the 2026 SOP. Last season the Kudremukh Wildlife Division shut every trekking route in Kudremukh NP, Someshwara and Mookambika sanctuaries from 14 January 2026 for forest-fire risk, 'until further notice'. Bags are checked, so leave plastic, packaged food and alcohol behind. Guides are compulsory: one per 10 under the 2026 SOP.

name: Narasimha Parvatha Trek
hook: Rainforest to grassy summit, with Barkana Falls on the long route.
why: Narasimha Parvatha (about 3,700 ft) is the high point above the Agumbe rainforest. The short loop from Kigga starts at the Rishyasringeshwara temple and is about 9 km. The full 15 km crossover from Mallanduru on the Agumbe side runs through rainforest, shola and grassland, and passes the top of Barkana Falls.
bestTime: Post-monsoon to winter.
seasonNote: Post-monsoon to December. The forest department closes these trails in the monsoon, and in 2026 it also shut them from 14 January for fire season, so treat late January onward as uncertain and check Aranya Vihaara before you plan.

trek.duration: Kigga–Kigga: about 9 km, easy to moderate. Mallanduru–Kigga crossover: about 15 km, moderate and a long day. Start by 7–7:30 AM (IndiaHikes).
trek.howToBook: Book on the Karnataka Forest Dept's Aranya Vihaara portal (aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in). Portal rules effective 15 Jul 2026: slots open up to 30 days ahead and must be booked at least 1 day ahead; cancel 8+ days out for a 50% refund, nothing back within 7 days; carry the original ID you booked with and report 10 minutes before your slot. Helpline 1926. The Kigga route is under Chikkamagaluru district treks, and the Mallanduru route under Shivamogga district treks (IndiaHikes).

bikeTips: Distance and time are to Kigga village, the trailhead near Sringeri, routed over the Agumbe ghat (NH169A, then SH27). Do the ghat in daylight both ways. Pair it with Sringeri darshan and the Peetham's annadana. The peak coordinates are in lat/lng.
safety: Forest sections are slippery, and mossy rocks at stream crossings are worse. Wear real trekking shoes. Stay on the marked trail. Flash photography and single-use plastic are banned in the trekking zones under the 2026 SOP. Last season the Kudremukh Wildlife Division shut every trekking route in Kudremukh NP, Someshwara and Mookambika sanctuaries from 14 January 2026 for forest-fire risk, 'until further notice'. Dry leaves make the forest descent slippery, so watch your knees and ankles. On the crossover, the rocks at the top of Barkana Falls on the Seetha River are very slippery. Stay well back from the edge.

name: Kundadri Hill & Jain Temple
hook: A 17th-century basadi, two rock pools, and wind.
why: Kundadri (826 m) is a forested hill near Agumbe topped by a 17th-century Jain temple to Parshwanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara. Tradition says Acharya Kundakunda sheltered here. Two small pools in the rock beside the temple once gave water to the sages. An all-weather road corkscrews to the top, and the summit looks out over the whole Malnad canopy.
bestTime: Clear winter mornings or late afternoons. Be down before dark.
seasonNote: Clear dry-season days bring the long views. The narrow hill road is slimy and dangerous in the monsoon.

trek.duration: Optional hike of about 7 km / 3 hours to the peak (Karnataka Tourism), or ride all the way up.
trek.howToBook: No booking found online. The road is open to private vehicles. Verify locally.

bikeTips: Take SH1 (Agumbe road) from the Thirthahalli side to Guddekeri, then the left turn-off to the hill (Wikipedia). Karnataka Tourism puts Agumbe 16 km away. The last stretch is steep and narrow with several hairpins. Ride it in first or second gear and don't attempt it on a weak scooter with a pillion.
safety: Steep, narrow climb with hairpins. Karnataka Tourism advises against it for inexperienced drivers. There are no facilities and no people at the top, so carry water and plan to be back in town before nightfall. Mind the drop-offs at the edge of the summit rocks.

name: Kemmanagundi, Z-Point & Hebbe Falls
hook: Old hill station, rose garden, and a 168 m two-step waterfall.
why: Kemmanagundi (about 1,434 m) is a Horticulture Department hill resort. Its Raj Bhavan guest house sits inside a botanical park full of roses. From there, a steep 45-minute climb past Shanti Falls takes you to Z-Point, a ridge-top lookout. Hebbe Falls drops 168 m in two stages, Dodda and Chikka Hebbe, about 7 km away down a jeep track.
bestTime: Post-monsoon, August to January, for Hebbe Falls (Karnataka Tourism).
seasonNote: August to January for Hebbe Falls (Karnataka Tourism); clearest views at Z-Point from November. By late January Hebbe thins.

trek.duration: Z-Point: about 45 minutes steep uphill from Raj Bhavan (Wikipedia). Hebbe Falls: about 7 km each way on foot or by local 4x4 jeep, plus a short hike (Karnataka Tourism).
trek.howToBook: No booking info found online. Local 4x4 jeeps run to Hebbe (Karnataka Tourism). Fares and current operating status: verify locally.

bikeTips: A long ride: 195 km and about 3h25m by OSRM, crossing the Agumbe ghat. Overnight in Chikkamagaluru or Kemmanagundi. Wikipedia puts Kemmanagundi 53 km from Chikkamagaluru and 17 km from Lingadahalli. Don't take a road bike down the Hebbe jeep track. Park it and take a jeep or walk. Combine with Mullayanagiri and Baba Budangiri.
safety: Long ghat sections both ways, so avoid night riding. Z-Point is a steep, exposed climb, so watch your footing and the edges in wind or mist. At Hebbe the rocks are slippery, and Karnataka Tourism warns about leeches and slick rock in the rains. Hebbe is inside a coffee estate in the eastern part of Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary (Wikipedia), so respect estate and forest rules.

name: Mullayanagiri & Seethalayanagiri
hook: Karnataka's rooftop. Book the slot, then climb 464 steps.
why: At about 1,925–1,930 m, Mullayanagiri is the highest peak in Karnataka. Wikipedia calls it the fourth-highest between the Himalayas and the Nilgiris. A road runs nearly to the top, then 464 steps lead to the small Mullappa Swamy shrine at the summit. Seethalayanagiri, the peak beside it, and the old Sarpadhari trail give you a way up on foot.
bestTime: Clear winter mornings. Take the 6 AM slot for visibility and thinner crowds.
seasonNote: Cold, clear mornings from October to February. Vehicle passes are booked online by slot (from September 2025). In the monsoon it's fogged in and the road is risky.

trek.duration: 464 steps from the road-end to the summit (Wikipedia). The Sarpadhari trail is the older walking route (no current details found).
trek.howToBook: Every vehicle needs an online entry pass from the Chikkamagaluru district tourism site (chikkamagaluru.nic.in/en/tourism; a 2025 local guide points to pgbiz.omniware.in/chikkamagalurutourism). Two slots: 6 AM–12 noon and 1–6 PM, 600 vehicles per slot, pre-booked vehicles first. Fees (Aug 2025): ₹50 bike, ₹100 car. This covers the Chandradrona range: Mullayanagiri, Seethalayyanagiri, Baba Budan dargah and Manikyadhara. Verify current rules.

bikeTips: OSRM's route is 181 km, about 3h20m, over the Agumbe ghat (NH169A to SH27) then NH173. Sleep in Chikkamagaluru the night before and ride up at dawn for the 6 AM slot. The summit road is narrow and single-lane in places. Carry your pass confirmation.
safety: Narrow hill road with blind corners and heavy weekend traffic. Use the horn and give way to vehicles coming down. The summit is windy and cold in winter mornings, so layer up. Fog can drop visibility to a few metres. Avoid riding back down the ghats after dark.

name: Kavaledurga Fort
hook: Keladi's last hilltop capital, swallowed by forest and mist.
why: Kavaledurga was the Keladi Nayakas' fortress. Queen Chennamma rallied her forces here in 1677, and Maratha prince Rajaram hid here from Aurangzeb in 1689. You walk through paddy fields, then up through three concentric granite walls, past a stepped tank, palace plinths and the Kashi Vishwanath and Srikanteshwara shrines. Built into the boulders, it still feels like a hideout.
bestTime: Winter mornings. Start early: entry hours are reported as early as 6 AM–2 PM, and Karnataka Tourism says entry closes by 5 PM.
seasonNote: Cool air for the climb and clear views from October to March. Green and dramatic in the monsoon, but the rock steps are slippery.

trek.duration: About 5 km round trip, half a day. Allow 2–3 hours to explore (IndiaHikes, Karnataka Tourism).
trek.howToBook: No permit. Buy a ticket at the checkpost (₹50 per IndiaHikes; ₹25 in a 2022 blog; parking around ₹20). Verify locally.

bikeTips: Ride over the Agumbe ghat towards Thirthahalli. The fort is about 18 km from Thirthahalli (Wikipedia, Karnataka Tourism). Park at the base and pick up a ticket at the checkpost. Pairs well with Kuppalli or Kundadri on the same day.
safety: Granite steps and boulder sections get slippery when wet. The topmost portion was reported closed to visitors in Aug 2024. No plastic or packed food inside, and drones are banned (bags are checked). Facilities are minimal, a tea shop by the parking at most, so carry water. Don't stay up for sunset if it means riding the ghat in the dark.

name: Kuppalli: Kuvempu's Kavimane & Kavishaila
hook: The poet's childhood home, and a Stonehenge built for him.
why: Kuvempu, the Kannada poet, grew up in this house. His family trust has turned it into the Kavimane museum. Up the hill, Kavishaila is a ring of megalithic rocks modelled on Stonehenge, with his memorial at the centre. Nearby is a rock signed by Kuvempu, B. M. Srikantaiah and T. S. Venkannaiah, which Poornachandra Tejaswi later signed too.
bestTime: Any season. Mornings are quieter.
seasonNote: Any season; the museum is indoors. Winter is pleasant for the walk up to Kavishaila, and the monsoon is lush.
bikeTips: Over the Agumbe ghat and on past Thirthahalli. Karnataka Tourism puts Kuppalli 31 km from Kundadri, so a Kundadri–Kuppalli–Kavaledurga loop works on one bike day.
safety: Short uphill walk to Kavishaila on rock, which can be slippery when damp. No photography inside the house museum. The ghat ride back should be done before dark.

name: Sakrebyle Elephant Camp
hook: Morning bath time for a herd of trained elephants.
why: On the Shivamogga–Thirthahalli road, Sakrebyle is a forest department camp where elephants are trained. Mornings are when the elephants are bathed and fed, and you can watch from close range. Get there by 8:30 or you'll only catch them drying off.

train.notes: Karnataka Tourism says the camp is 14 km from Shimoga, but there's no sensible direct rail link from Udupi. Ride instead.

bestTime: Early morning, by 8:30 AM.
seasonNote: Elephant bathing is in the early morning (by about 8:30 AM) year-round. In the monsoon the river is high, so verify that the camp is open.
bikeTips: OSRM routes it over the Agumbe ghat via Thirthahalli on NH169A/NH169: 126 km, about 1h50m. The morning window is short (8:30–11:30 AM per karnataka.com), so a dawn start or an overnight stop is the only way to see the bath.
safety: Elephants are wild animals, trained or not. Keep the distance the mahouts set, don't feed them unless invited, and never stand behind one. The ground at the bathing spot is wet and slippery. A pre-dawn ghat ride means fog and low light, so ride slow with lights on.

name: Jog Falls
hook: Raja, Rani, Roarer, Rocket: a 253 m drop.
why: The Sharavathi drops 253 m at Jog in four named strands: Raja, Rani, Roarer and Rocket. Karnataka Tourism calls it India's second-highest plunge waterfall. The main deck at Kargal gives the full panorama, and a viewing tower opened in 2025. The British Bungalow looks across from the Siddapur side. About 1,400 steps lead to the base when they're open.

train.notes: Talaguppa is 13–18 km from the falls, but it's on the Shivamogga line, not the Konkan Railway. No sensible rail route from Udupi.

bestTime: August to December. Karnataka Tourism rates October–December best overall.
seasonNote: August to December, with October–December rated best by Karnataka Tourism. Flow depends on releases from the Linganamakki dam; by January it's "moderate". In peak monsoon it can be completely clouded.
bikeTips: 161 km, about 2h45m by OSRM, up the NH66 coast and then SH50 inland. Do it as an overnight: sleep in Jog, Sagara or by the Linganamakki backwaters. Parking is ₹30 for two-wheelers. Entry ₹20 (Indians), and visits are capped at 2 hours. Hours are 7:30 AM–9:30 PM (Karnataka Tourism).
safety: The 1,400-step trek to the base is tough (45–60 minutes each way). Karnataka Tourism says it's often restricted for safety, so check on site and never go past barriers. Stay behind viewpoint railings, because the gorge edge is sheer. The Watkins Platform near the base depends on water levels and safety rules. Patchy phone signal, and the nearest hospital is in Sagara, about 30 km away. Drones need a ₹500 ticket.

name: Baba Budangiri (Inam Dattatreya Peetha)
hook: Where India's first coffee seeds are said to have been planted.
why: The Chandradrona range is where Baba Budan is said to have brought coffee from Mocha, Yemen, starting India's coffee story. His cave shrine is revered by both Hindus and Muslims as the Dattatreya Peetha and Baba Budan dargah. Manikyadhara Falls tumbles down the same hillside.
bestTime: Clear winter mornings. Book the 6 AM slot.
seasonNote: Clear winter mornings; book the same online vehicle slot as Mullayanagiri. Datta Jayanti (December) brings large crowds and tight security.
bikeTips: Same approach as Mullayanagiri: overnight in Chikkamagaluru, then an online vehicle pass for the 6 AM–12 or 1–6 PM slot (₹50 bike, Aug 2025). 189 km and about 3h35m from Manipal (OSRM).
safety: Narrow hill road with weekend traffic, fog and cold mornings. Follow police and shrine instructions. Manikyadhara's rocks are slippery.

name: Ayyanakere Lake
hook: A Hoysala-era tank still watering fields, Shakunagiri behind.
why: Ayyanakere, near Sakharayapatna, is an old irrigation lake that local tradition credits to Rukmangada Raya, renovated by the Hoysalas in 1156. It still feeds about 1,560 hectares through ten canals. Shakunagiri hill rises behind the water, and there are almost no tourist facilities, which is half the point.
bestTime: Post-monsoon, when the tank is fuller. Mornings for soft light.
seasonNote: Fullest after the monsoon; soft morning light in winter. Only worth it if you're already in Chikkamagaluru.
bikeTips: 189 km / about 3h15m from Manipal (OSRM). Treat it as an add-on from Chikkamagaluru town, 18 km away.
safety: No facilities or lifeguards. Don't swim in the tank, and keep off the slippery bund edges. Carry water.

name: Murudeshwar Temple & Beach
hook: A giant Shiva, a 20-storey gopura and the sea at your feet
why: The temple sits on a headland with the Arabian Sea on three sides, and one of the world's tallest Shiva statues watches over the bay. Take the lift up the 20-storey Raja Gopura for the full view: temple, town, fishing boats and Netrani on the horizon. Then walk down for free anna prasada and a sunset on the sand.

train.notes: Murdeshwar has its own Konkan Railway station (Karnataka Tourism). Check stops for your train on NTES/IRCTC; the Karnataka Tourism page says Vande Bharat services stop at nearby stations, not Murdeshwar itself. Auto from station to temple; distance not verified, verify locally.

bestTime: Oct–Mar; weekday early mornings are least crowded (Karnataka Tourism). Avoid Maha Shivaratri unless you want the crowds.
seasonNote: October–March for the beach (Karnataka Tourism); the temple is open year-round. Maha Shivaratri is the big crush. Monsoon (June–September): rough sea, red flags, no swimming, and boats and water sports stop. The beach was closed after drownings in December 2024 and reopened with ropes.
vegFoodNearby: Temple Anna Prasada (free, served in the afternoon, subject to availability; Karnataka Tourism)

temple.dressCode: Inner areas: men in dhoti/panche or full-length formal trousers; women in saree or salwar kameez/churidar with dupatta. No shorts, sleeveless tops, ripped jeans, T-shirts or skirts in the inner areas (dress code notified June 2025). Footwear off at the entrance; no photography inside the sanctum.
temple.darshanTimings: 6:00 AM–1:00 PM and 3:00 PM–8:30 PM; abhisheka from 6:30 AM. Timings change on festival days (Karnataka Tourism).
temple.annadana: Free anna prasada served daily in the afternoon, subject to availability; exact start time not published, verify locally.

bikeTips: NH66 north all the way through Kundapura, Byndoor and Bhatkal. Straight, fast, flat, but crowded with buses and trucks. Park near the temple approach. Lift fee for the gopura is small (about ₹10–20 per Karnataka Tourism). Bring a dhoti or formal trousers in your tank bag.
safety: Murudeshwar beach was closed after four schoolgirls drowned on 10 Dec 2024 when a wave hit them; it reopened around 26 Dec 2024 with shoreline safety ropes. Stay inside the roped zone, do not swim beyond waist depth, and obey lifeguards. Use only certified water-sports operators and wear a life jacket. NH66 has heavy truck/bus traffic; avoid night riding.

name: Netrani Island (snorkelling & scuba from Murudeshwar)
hook: Karnataka's heart-shaped dive island, 19 km out to sea
why: Netrani is a rocky, heart-shaped island off Murudeshwar, ringed with coral and fish. You don't land on it: boats moor offshore and you snorkel or dive along the reef. The boat ride out is about 1.5 hours each way, so this is a full, salty, sunburnt day.

train.notes: Dive boats leave from Murudeshwar; ride or take the train to Murdeshwar station and confirm pickup point with your operator.

bestTime: Nov–May, strictly outside the monsoon (Karnataka Tourism); operators have been allowed to dive Oct–Apr per district rules (reported).
seasonNote: Diving season is about November to May, strictly outside the monsoon (Karnataka Tourism); visibility varies day to day.
vegFoodNearby: Murudeshwar temple anna prasada on your way back (free, afternoon, subject to availability; Karnataka Tourism)
bikeTips: Distance and time are to Murudeshwar (the departure point); the island itself is about 19 km offshore and roughly 1.5 h by boat. Reach Murudeshwar by 7:30 AM; operators confirm the jetty. Carry photo ID.
safety: Public landing on Netrani is prohibited: Karnataka Tourism calls it a restricted naval area, and earlier reports say casual visitors need coastal police permission (operators handle paperwork). The Navy historically used it for target practice. Only dive with a certified operator; PADI minimum age for diving is 10. Trips stop completely June–September. Sea-sickness on the 1.5 h crossing is common.

name: Idagunji Maha Ganapathi Temple
hook: Honnavar's beloved Ganapati, a short hop off NH66
why: One of the coast's best-loved Ganapati shrines, a few kilometres inland from Honnavar. Doors open at 6 AM and the abhisheka crowd builds fast. Pair it with Murudeshwar and Apsarakonda for a tidy coastal temple-and-waterfall day.

train.notes: Both are Konkan Railway stops near Idagunji; which is closer and the onward auto fare were not verified online, verify locally.

bestTime: Oct–Feb mornings; festival days are crowded.
seasonNote: Open year-round; October to February mornings are most comfortable. Festival days are crowded.

temple.dressCode: Traditional, formal clothing expected (Yatradham); men are advised dhoti or trousers, no shorts. No photography.
temple.darshanTimings: 6:00 AM–1:00 PM and 3:00 PM–8:30 PM (Yatradham). One listing gives a 4 PM evening start, verify locally.
temple.annadana: Not confirmed as a daily free meal online. Prasada is available, and a donor-sponsored Shashwatha Annadana seva exists. Verify locally (temple office 08387 247227).

bikeTips: NH66 to Honnavar side, then the short turn inland to Idagunji. Easy, flat ride. Combine with Apsarakonda (a few km away) and Murudeshwar on the way back.
safety: NH66 traffic is heavy and fast; avoid riding after dark. Temple area gets congested on Sankashti and festival days.

name: Gokarna Mahabaleshwar Temple
hook: Touch the Atmalinga yourself, then eat with the town
why: An ancient Dravidian-style Shiva temple facing Gokarna beach, home to the Atmalinga. Devotees can enter the sanctum, touch the linga and do abhisheka with their own hands. Come shirtless in a dhoti, then join the free Amrutanna bhojana: rice, rasam, sambar, buttermilk, payasa.

train.notes: Gokarna Road station is about 9 km from the temple; autos and taxis available (Karnataka Tourism).

bestTime: Oct–Mar. Maha Shivaratri is the big festival; book early if you go then.
seasonNote: Open year-round. Maha Shivaratri (February–March) is the biggest festival, with chariot processions and huge crowds; book stays early.
vegFoodNearby: Amrutanna Prasad Bhojana at the temple (free, 12:00–2:00 PM and 7:30–8:30 PM; temple trust site)

temple.dressCode: Men: dhoti only, shirt, T-shirt and vest removed (bare-chested); no jeans, trousers, shorts, hats. Women: saree or salwar suit, no jeans/pants. Rule announced Oct 2018; Karnataka Tourism still describes shirt removal for the sanctum. No photography inside.
temple.darshanTimings: 6:00 AM–12:30 PM and 5:00 PM–8:00 PM (Mangalarti at 8 PM); open daily. Hours shift on festivals, Mondays and Shivaratri (Karnataka Tourism).
temple.annadana: Free Amrutanna Prasad Bhojana twice daily: 12:00–2:00 PM and 7:30–8:30 PM (Shri Mahabaleshwara Deva trust).

bikeTips: NH66 north past Murudeshwar, Honnavar and Kumta, then the Gokarna turn-off. Vehicles are not allowed near the temple: park and walk about 10 minutes along Car Street. Carry a dhoti.
safety: Narrow, crowded Car Street; watch your bag. NH66 Honnavar–Kumta stretch has heavy trucks; avoid night riding.

name: Gokarna beach trail: Kudle, Om, Half Moon & Paradise
hook: Four coves, one cliff path, and a boat back
why: Start at Kudle, climb over the headland to Om, then follow the jungle path off Om's southern end to Half Moon (about 30 minutes) and on to the last cove beyond. No electricity at the far beaches, just shacks, cliffs and very blue water. Walk out in the morning, catch a boat back to Om when your legs say so.

train.notes: Gokarna Road station is about 9 km from town (Karnataka Tourism); autos/taxis to Kudle or Om.

bestTime: Oct–Mar; mornings have calmer seas. Bioluminescence at the far cove is best on new-moon nights (Karnataka Tourism).
seasonNote: Prime season is October to March; mornings have calmer seas. Monsoon (June–September): rough sea, red flags, no swimming, and boats and water sports stop. The cliff paths turn dangerous in the rain.
vegFoodNearby: Mahabaleshwar temple Amrutanna Prasad Bhojana in town (free, 12–2 PM & 7:30–8:30 PM; temple trust site)
bikeTips: Lat/lng and distance are for Om Beach parking. Kudle and Om have road access, parking and toilets; Half Moon and the last cove are walk-or-boat only. Leave the bike at Om and don't ride the beach roads after dark.
safety: Drownings are recurring around Gokarna: two MBBS students were swept away watching sunset near Jatayu Teertha, Kudle, in April 2025. No dated Om-specific drowning report was found online, but Karnataka Tourism says Om's water can be rough. At Half Moon, currents are strong and drownings have happened (Holidify); at Paradise Beach avoid swimming entirely: sharp rocks and strong undercurrents (Karnataka Tourism). Stick to marked trails; cliff edges are slippery; never walk the trail after sunset or in the monsoon. Boat activities are suspended June–Sept; use operators with life jackets. No closure order for Half Moon or Paradise found online; verify locally.

name: Karwar town & Rabindranath Tagore Beach
hook: A navy town's promenade, with a missile boat parked on the sand
why: Karwar sits where the Kali river meets the sea, and its long town beach carries Rabindranath Tagore's name. The decommissioned missile boat INS Chapal sits on the beach as a museum. Good overnight base for Devbagh or an early run to Dudhsagar.

train.notes: Karwar station is a Konkan Railway stop a few km from town; check stopping trains on NTES/IRCTC. The 70101/70102 Madgaon–Karwar MEMU runs daily (Konkan Railway list).

bestTime: Oct–Mar; evenings for the promenade.
seasonNote: Pleasant evenings on the promenade from October to March. Monsoon (June–September): rough sea, red flags, no swimming, and boats and water sports stop.
bikeTips: NH66 north from Gokarna via Ankola. Overnight here if you're heading to Collem for Dudhsagar (87 km, about 1h 45m by OSRM). INS Chapal museum hours and fee vary by source (commonly 10 AM–1 PM and about 4:30–6 PM, about ₹15), verify locally.
safety: Town beach: swim only where lifeguards are present; none confirmed online, verify locally. Naval areas around Karwar are off-limits; obey signs and don't photograph naval installations.

name: Devbagh Beach & Kali River Mouth
hook: Casuarina sandbar where the Kali river runs into the sea
why: A long strip of sand and casuarina groves at the mouth of the Kali, about 6 km from Karwar, reached by a short boat ride across the river. Jungle Lodges & Resorts runs a beach resort here. Sunrise over the river, sunset over the sea, same day.

train.notes: Karwar station is about 6 km away (Karnataka Tourism); auto to the jetty, then boat.

bestTime: Oct–Mar.
seasonNote: Calm, shallow water from October to March. Monsoon (June–September): rough sea, red flags, no swimming, and boats and water sports stop.
bikeTips: Distance/time are to Devbagh jetty near the Kali bridge on NH66. Boat departure point and transfer arrangements vary by source (JLR office in Karwar, Karwar dock, or the jetty near Kali bridge); confirm with Jungle Lodges when booking. Bike stays on the mainland.
safety: Karnataka Tourism calls the water calm and shallow, but the river mouth has currents; don't swim near it. Use operators with life jackets for water sports. Carry insect repellent in the casuarinas.

name: Mirjan Fort
hook: The Pepper Queen's moss-green laterite fort
why: Built by Rani Chennabhairadevi, the 16th-century 'Queen of Pepper', this laterite fort has four gates, moats and underground passages. In winter the walls are green with moss and the place is near-silent. Ten minutes off NH66, an hour well spent.

train.notes: Kumta station is about 12 km away; autos and taxis available (Karnataka Tourism).

bestTime: Oct–Feb; mornings.
seasonNote: Dry paths and soft light from October to February. It's lushest (and mossiest) just after the monsoon.
bikeTips: About 0.5 km off NH66 between Kumta and Gokarna. Bring water and snacks; nothing nearby to buy.
safety: Uneven laterite steps and slippery moss; watch your footing on walls. Avoid heavy rain. Hours listed as 9 AM–5 PM, free entry (Karnataka Tourism); other listings say 8 AM–6 PM, verify locally.

name: Apsarakonda Falls
hook: Small falls, a pool and a sea view near NH66
why: A short drop into a pool in a forest park near Honnavar, with Pandava caves and a viewpoint over the sea close by. It's small, but the combination of falls, caves and coast in one stop makes it worth the detour.

train.notes: Apsarakonda is about 8 km from Honnavar bus stand (Wikipedia); auto from town.

bestTime: Monsoon and just after for flow; winter for comfort.
seasonNote: Water from the monsoon until about November; by winter it's a trickle. Go for the caves and the sea view in the dry months.
bikeTips: Turn off NH66 near Honnavar; last stretch is a village road. Pair with Idagunji and Kasarkod Eco Beach.
safety: Steps (roughly 100–150 per a blog) are slippery when wet. Swimming rules not confirmed officially; verify locally before getting in. Fee and hours vary by source, verify locally.

name: Yana Rocks
hook: Two black karst towers rising out of the forest
why: Bhairaveshwara Shikhara (about 120 m) and Mohini Shikhara are jet-black karst monoliths in the Sahyadri forest, with a cave temple where spring water drips on a Shiva linga. The squeeze through the cave passage is the highlight. GSI declared the site a National Geological Monument in 2026 (Wikipedia).

train.notes: Kumta station is about 25–30 km away; local taxis and buses run to Yana (Karnataka Tourism).

bestTime: Oct–Mar; Nov–Feb peak; early mornings (Karnataka Tourism).
seasonNote: October to March, with November–February peak (Karnataka Tourism). The monsoon brings leeches and slippery trails.

trek.duration: 2–3 hours for the full circuit (about 260 steps to the monoliths plus cave steps)
trek.howToBook: No booking; pay the Forest Department eco-development fee (about ₹20–50 per person per Karnataka Tourism) and parking (₹20 two-wheeler) at the gate. Cash only.

bikeTips: From Kumta take the Sirsi road via Hiregutti/Mattighatta side; the Mattighatta approach has a short paved walk (500 m–1 km). Final roads are narrow forest roads; ride in daylight. Open 8 AM–6 PM.
safety: Remove footwear at the base counter before the cave passage (Karnataka Tourism), so carry socks or wipes. Wear grippy shoes on the trail. Steep, uneven cave steps. Plastic deposit system in force. Forest road: watch for wildlife and don't ride after dark.

name: Sathodi Falls
hook: A wide, short falls spilling into the Kali backwaters
why: A broad, rectangular 15 m curtain of water in the forest near Yellapur that feeds the backwaters of the Kodasalli dam on the Kali. The pool below is shallow enough that it looks like an invitation. Remote, rough road, worth it for the drama.

train.notes: Nearest railhead per Karnataka Tourism is Hubballi (97 km); not practical from Udupi.

bestTime: Nov–Apr per Trawell; avoid monsoon (slippery, and entry has been restricted when the Kali swells).
seasonNote: November to April per Trawell. Entry has been restricted when the Kali river swells in the monsoon (closed June 2025).
bikeTips: From Yellapur take the Hubli highway and turn towards Ganeshgudi; the last stretch is poor and better with ground clearance (Trawell). Walk the final 0.5 km from the gate. Coordinates from Wikipedia; OSRM routes to the nearest road point.
safety: Rough forest road; ride only in daylight and carry fuel. Wet rocks are extremely slippery; don't climb on the falls. The Forest Dept restricted entry in June 2025 when Kali water levels rose. Entry about ₹5 and 6 AM–5 PM per Trawell; current status and fee verify locally.

name: Magod Falls
hook: The Bedthi drops about 200 m in two steps into a gorge
why: The Bedthi river plunges nearly 200 m in two stages into a deep, forested gorge. A handrailed walkway leads from the parking to the viewpoint, so it's all view, no scramble. Jenukallu Gudda viewpoint is 4 km away for sunset.

train.notes: Nearest railhead is Hubballi (86 km per Karnataka Tourism); not practical from Udupi.

bestTime: Jul–Dec (Karnataka Tourism); minimal water in summer.
seasonNote: July to December (Karnataka Tourism); minimal water in summer.
bikeTips: About 17 km from Yellapur town. Combine with Sathodi and Sirsi in a two-night Yellapur–Sirsi loop. Open 9 AM–6 PM (Karnataka Tourism).
safety: Stay behind the handrails; the gorge edge is sheer. Ghat and forest roads around Yellapur carry heavy trucks on the Hubli highway; avoid night riding. Entry fee not stated officially, verify locally.

name: Vibhuti Falls
hook: A forest falls and stream crossing, minutes from Yana
why: A short forest walk (a paved path, then a rocky trail with stream crossings) leads to a tall falls over limestone near Yana. Easy to do the same morning as Yana Rocks.

train.notes: Kumta (Konkan Railway) is the nearest station but needs a taxi on poor roads; distance not verified.

bestTime: Monsoon and Oct–Jan for flow; winter for comfort.
seasonNote: Flows through the monsoon and into early winter, thinner by January. Best as a Yana add-on.
bikeTips: From Kumta via Hiregutti is the better road; the road from Yana is bad (eNidhi blog). Parking is close to the trailhead. Carry food and water; no canteen near the falls.
safety: Signs prohibit entering the pool and trekking uphill; obey them. Rocky, slippery path with stream crossings. Fee about ₹10 and hours roughly 9 AM–5 PM per a 2020 blog, verify locally.

name: Dandeli & Kali River Rafting
hook: Whitewater on the Kali, hornbills over the camp
why: Dandeli sits on the Kali river inside hornbill country, and the rafting stretch from Ganeshgudi below Supa Dam is the Kali's commercial whitewater run. Short, mid and long runs are on offer, with the long run covering 9–12 km. Mornings are for birding; afternoons for the river.

train.notes: No sensible Konkan Railway approach; nearest major railhead is Hubballi or Dharwad (verify locally).

bestTime: Rafting runs roughly Oct–Jun depending on Supa Dam releases and forest clearance (Karnataka Tourism); suspended in the rains.
seasonNote: Rafting runs roughly October to June, depending on Supa Dam releases and forest clearance, and stops in the rains. As of January 2026 the long-run licence was under challenge, so verify locally.
bikeTips: Long day: about 5 hours from Manipal via the coast and the ghat roads. Split it with a night in Sirsi or Yellapur. Ganeshgudi (rafting launch area) is about 308 km from Manipal by OSRM.
safety: Raft only with operators that provide life jackets, helmets and trained river guides (mandatory per Karnataka Tourism). Age and weight limits vary by operator (commonly 12–14+ for long runs), verify locally. Rafting is inside the Hornbill Conservation Reserve / tiger reserve area: no off-road wandering, and wildlife on roads at dawn and dusk. Ghat roads: hairpins, trucks, fog in early mornings; don't ride after dark. Veg-friendly stays not verified online; ask resorts for pure-veg meals and verify locally.

name: Sirsi Marikamba Temple
hook: Sirsi's fierce goddess, and a jatre every two years
why: The Marikamba temple is Sirsi's heart and the seat of one of Karnataka's biggest temple fairs, held once every two years. On normal days it's a busy town temple; on jatre years the whole town turns into a fair ground.

train.notes: Nearest railhead is Hubballi Junction (Bhakti Bharat); from the coast, Kumta (Konkan Railway) plus a bus up the ghat is possible, verify locally.

bestTime: October to February. The Marikamba Jatre is held every two years: it last ran 24 Feb–4 Mar 2026, and the next is due in 2028 (Wikipedia).
seasonNote: Open year-round. The Marikamba Jatre is held every two years (last 24 Feb–4 Mar 2026; next due 2028).

temple.darshanTimings: 7:00 AM–9:00 PM, all week (Bhakti Bharat; single source, verify locally).
temple.annadana: Not confirmed online — verify locally. Prasad is available.

bikeTips: Ride up from Kumta via the Devimane ghat or from Honnavar; ghat sections have hairpins and buses. Stay the night in Sirsi.
safety: Ghat roads to Sirsi: hairpins, buses, morning fog. Avoid night riding. Dress code not published online; wear traditional clothes to be safe (verify locally).

name: Dudhsagar Falls (overnight via Konkan Railway + Collem jeep safari)
hook: Night train to Goa, forest jeep to a 310 m milk-white falls
why: Dudhsagar is a four-tier, 310 m falls on the Mahadayi river, and the Belagavi–Vasco railway line runs right past it. The legal way in is the official jeep safari from Collem: a bumpy forest track, river crossings, then a walk to the pool. Do it by night train from Udupi and you're at the gate by 9 AM.

train.notes: UDUPI -> MADGAON (Konkan Railway). Daily options (timings from etrain.info listing, Nov 2026; confirm on NTES/IRCTC): 16346 Netravati Exp dep Udupi 00:22, arr Madgaon 04:35; 12134 Mangaluru–CSMT SF Exp dep 15:18, arr 18:40; 12620 Matsyagandha Exp dep 15:50, arr 20:00; 12617 Mangala Lakshadweep Exp dep 23:06, arr 03:00. Also 20646 Vande Bharat dep 09:50, arr 13:10 (not daily). MADGAON -> KULEM (Collem, QLM), South Western Railway, daily passengers: 56962 dep Madgaon 08:10, arr Kulem 09:15; 56964 dep 13:40, arr 14:55; 56966 dep 18:12, arr 19:25. RETURN Kulem -> Madgaon: 56961 dep 06:30 arr 07:18; 56963 dep 12:20 arr 13:08; 56965 dep 17:20 arr 18:10. Madgaon -> Udupi: 12618 Mangala dep 16:10 arr 20:20; 20645 Vande Bharat dep 18:10 arr 21:12 (not daily); 16345 Netravati dep 22:42 arr 03:00; 12619 Matsyagandha dep 01:15 arr 05:18. SUGGESTED PLAN A (one night on the train): Netravati 16346 out of Udupi at 00:22 -> breakfast at Madgaon -> 56962 to Kulem by 09:15 -> jeep safari -> 56965 at 17:20 -> Madgaon 18:10 -> Netravati 16345 at 22:42 -> Udupi 03:00. PLAN B (hotel night): Matsyagandha 12620 at 15:50 -> Madgaon 20:00, sleep in Margao -> 56962 next morning. Kulem station is in Collem village; the jeep counter location is not documented online, verify locally. NEVER get off at Dudhsagar station or any Braganza Ghat stop and never walk the tracks.

bestTime: Jeep safari season opens after the monsoon (early October; 2026–27 season opened early Oct 2026 per a forest department order reported by Curly Tales) and runs until the monsoon closure.
seasonNote: The official jeep safari runs after the monsoon, from about October (the 2026–27 season opened in early October). The falls are fullest right after the rains. Closed in the monsoon. Walking the railway tracks is prohibited in every season.

trek.duration: Half day from Collem (jeep ride plus a short walk to the pool); exact durations verify locally
trek.howToBook: Book an authorised Forest Department-registered jeep through the GTDC (Goa Tourism Development Corporation) online portal; the exact portal URL was not confirmable from an official page, so get it from goa-tourism / GTDC channels and don't pay unverified sites. Collem gate runs 8 AM–3 PM, batches of 30–40 hourly, max 240 trips/day, 7 adults per jeep. Fee: Outlook Traveller cited about ₹500 per passenger in 2023; current 2026–27 fee not confirmed, verify locally.

bikeTips: Route breaks overnight. Option 1: Manipal -> Gokarna (179 km, ~3h 05m), sleep, then Gokarna -> Collem (134 km, ~2h 45m). Option 2: push to Karwar (215 km, ~3h 45m), sleep, then Karwar -> Collem (87 km, ~1h 45m) to make the 8 AM gate. Two-wheelers and private vehicles are NOT allowed into the safari circuit: park at Collem and take the jeep. Total Manipal -> Kulem is 302 km by OSRM.
safety: Walking on the railway tracks or bridge to Dudhsagar is prohibited: South Western Railway bars public access via the railway route, and RPF (Hubballi Division, Castle Rock post) fined 32 tourists ₹500 each under Section 147 of the Railways Act in July 2026; a South Goa Collector's order (2023) bans entry by train or on foot along the track and has RPF stop people de-boarding near Dudhsagar. Inside the circuit: life jackets are mandatory at the falls, no plastic bottles/bags, no alcohol, and trips can be suspended on orange/red weather alerts. Rocks at the pool are slippery. If riding, don't do Anmod/forest roads at night.

name: Kasarkod Eco Beach & Sharavathi Mangrove Boardwalk
hook: A Blue Flag beach, then a boardwalk through Sharavathi mangroves
why: Kasarkod is one of India's Blue Flag certified beaches: 5 km of clean sand with proper facilities. Across the road, the Sharavathi Kandla mangrove boardwalk takes you into the estuary where the river meets the sea. A calm, family-easy stop between Idagunji and Apsarakonda.

train.notes: Honnavar has direct trains from Mangalore and Goa (Karnataka Tourism); short auto ride to the beach, distance verify locally.

bestTime: Oct–Feb (Karnataka Tourism, Honnavar guide).
seasonNote: October–February (Karnataka Tourism). Monsoon (June–September): rough sea, red flags, no swimming, and boats and water sports stop.
bikeTips: Just off NH66 at Honnavar. Fold into a Murudeshwar–Idagunji–Apsarakonda–Kasarkod loop and be home by dark.
safety: Blue Flag beaches have designated swim zones; swim only in them and follow lifeguards (specific timings not published, verify locally). Boardwalk can be slick after rain.

name: Basavaraj Durga Island Fort
hook: A laterite island fort off Honnavar, reached only by boat
why: A small island off Honnavar ringed by laterite fortification walls, named after the Keladi prince Basavaraja after Shivappa Nayaka took it. Rusting cannon and sea on every side. Getting there is the adventure, and access is not guaranteed.

train.notes: From Honnavar, boat to the island; departure point and boatmen not verified, verify locally.

bestTime: Oct–May; not in the monsoon.
seasonNote: October to May only, never in the monsoon. Whether you can land depends on local permission; one report says only at Sankranti. Verify locally in Honnavar.
bikeTips: Distance and time are to Honnavar town (the boat side); the island is about 4–7 km offshore. Ask at Honnavar port/riverfront for a boat.
safety: Access is uncertain: some listings say landing is only allowed at Sankranti with local permission. Never take an unlicensed boat without life jackets. Fort walls are crumbling; watch the edges.
